data.name: Aaima
data.gender_notes: Aaima is used as a unisex name in Islamic naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: The name Aaima is derived from Arabic origin and is the name of the mother of Aisha (R.A.), one of the wives of Prophet Muhammad (PBUH). This name signifies a deep connection and love towards the Prophet and his family. The name Aaima carries the meaning “Mother of Aisha” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in Arabic, Urdu, Persian. Parents who choose Aaima usually hope their child will grow to embody mother of aisha and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.etymology: Aaima belongs to the Arabic linguistic tradition and is used in Islamic naming. Its recorded meaning is “Mother of Aisha.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Aaima total 7, giving a life-path number of 7. Number 7 is linked with Ketu and with the qualities of reflection, wisdom and inner depth.

The name has been passed down through generations, and it serves as a reminder of the importance of family and motherly love in Islamic culture.
data.spiritual_significance: From a spiritual perspective, the name Aaima symbolizes deep devotion and love towards Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) and his family. The name Aaima also emphasizes the idea of unwavering love and support towards one's family and the prophetic family, which is a fundamental aspect of the Islamic faith.
